title: QUANTITY OF ENGLISH FINE BONE ...
description: QUANTITY OF ENGLISH FINE BONE CHINA TRIOS & DUOS
findings: About nine sets (roughly 25 pieces) across three photos, which supports the title of English fine bone china trios and duos. Marks read: on the cream-ground pink rose-garland trio at left in photo 2, the cup base carries a printed Royal Doulton lion-and-crown backstamp in green and gold with a 'D' pattern number beside it (digits only partly legible, looks like D5...). A second rose-garland trio in a near identical pattern has a different small green printed pictorial mark (small figure, text illegible), so its maker is unconfirmed. A trio with one large pink cabbage rose on the cup has a purple script pattern-name backstamp with two roses (name illegible; the style fits Royal Albert type rose patterns but that is not confirmed). Also seen: a cup and snack plate (tennis set) with pink cabbage roses, a pale green Art Deco style trio with a yellow lined cup, roses inside and an enamelled floral pedestal foot, a pink edged fluted white trio with tiny sprigs, a daisy and mixed flower trio with gilt rims, a Victorian or Edwardian embossed plate on a stand with matching cup and saucer in pale blue and yellow sprays and a gilt flecked rim, and a primrose cup and saucer with worn gilt edge. No marks seen on most of these. The title does not name Royal Doulton.
condition: No chips, cracks or crazing seen at this photo resolution, but several cups are inverted or on their sides so interiors are not all visible. Gilt rims show light wear; the embossed Victorian plate and the primrose saucer show worn gilt flecks.
reason: Mixed English bone china with at least one Royal Doulton rose-garland trio (lion-and-crown mark read) and probable Royal Albert style rose trios; about 25 pieces, likely $80-150 as a lot (my estimate).

title: BOX OF VINTAGE PERIODICALS & E...
findings: More than periodicals: the box holds Australian aviation and Sydney ephemera. (1) A printed 'In Memoriam' order of service card for Flight-Lieut. Keith Anderson (a line mentioning Royal Air Force is partly legible), Mosman Presbyterian Church, minister The Rev. D. P. Macdonald (ex-Chaplain A.I.F.), organist Dr Keith Barry (ex-Capt. 4th Dorsets, attached R.A.F.), dated '6th July 192?' (last digit unclear), 10.30 a.m., with a portrait photo. Keith Anderson was the Kookaburra pilot who died in the Tanami Desert in April 1929 while searching for Kingsford Smith; a web search snippet seen on 19/10/2026 put his burial at Mosman on 6 July 1929, which fits the card. (2) A newspaper clipping headed 'Maps and Radio. How News Will Come. Tracing the flight of a giant bird' with a pilot portrait (flight and date not confirmed). (3) A large colour print captioned 'The Sydney Harbour Bridge ... A Watercolour by J... A...' (artist name unreadable; the second line may refer to the bridge opening, March 1932, low confidence) and a large black and white print of a dense crowd with flags (caption illegible). (4) Three old Sydney newspapers: Sydney Morning Herald, Daily Telegraph and a masthead ending '...NING NEWS' (probably Evening News); dates not legible. (5) An open bound volume of a Boer War illustrated periodical (running head looks like 'BATTLE BOOK', low confidence) with a 'Soldiers' Letters' section and a photo page captioned 'Major Robin and Adjutant, New Zealand Contingent ... celebrated for his gallant ride of 1 1/2 miles under fire ('Spear.')'. (6) A LIFE International special double issue 'The World in Our Time: A Pictorial Atlas for the Space Age' and a furniture advertisement clipping (E. G. Glass, George Street). One web search found no sale record for the Anderson card, so its value is an estimate only.
condition: Typical aged paper: toned and browned newsprint, folds and creases, edge curling and small tears on the large prints, foxing on the bound volume; no missing pages seen on the open spread; LIFE issue looks fair.
reason: Under-described box with a 1929 Keith Anderson (Kookaburra) memorial order of service, Sydney Harbour Bridge print and newspapers, and a bound Boer War periodical volume; likely $120-300 to ephemera and aviation collectors (my estimate).

title: BLUE & WHITE PLATE & 4 BISQUE ...
findings: A large blue and white onion pattern (Zwiebelmuster style) dish with a scalloped rim and a hand-written number ending '142' on the rim edge (inventory style, not a maker mark). The base is not photographed, so Meissen or other factory marks cannot be checked; the pattern was made by Meissen and many other factories, so do not assume Meissen. Four pastel bisque figures, unmarked except for hand-lettered script on two bases: a bearded sailor waving a cloth with a spar under his arm, base script reads 'Distress' (fairly clear); a bearded fisherman with an anchor on his shirt holding a rope or net, base has a short script title (illegible); a boy in a feathered hat playing a guitar or mandolin; and a girl in a bonnet and striped apron. The style looks late 19th to early 20th century continental (probably German) bisque. No impressed numbers or factory marks seen (bases not photographed from underneath).
condition: Figures look intact in the photos with bright colour; no breaks seen, though small losses to fingers or props are not ruled out; the plate shows no cracks in the photos.
reason: Four antique looking continental bisque figures (two with script titles) plus a large blue onion dish; unmarked so value rests on age and maker; likely $80-200 (my estimate).
marks_read: Script 'Distress' on base of sailor figure; short script title on fisherman base (illegible); hand-written number ending 142 on plate rim; no factory marks seen
